Edward Bruce Moore (born December 25, 1851) was an American lawyer, journalist, and government official who served as the United States Commissioner of Patents from 1907 to 1913.
Early life and career
Moore was born in North Anson, Maine. As a teenager he moved to Washington, D.C., where he worked as a page in the United States Senate. He later became editor of the Washington Daily News and the Washington Daily Telegraph and was admitted to the bar in 1881.
Patent Office
Moore joined the Patent Office as an assistant examiner in 1883. He later served as law clerk, principal examiner, and assistant commissioner before becoming commissioner of patents in 1907. He also represented the United States in international patent-related meetings, including the Paris Exposition of 1900 and the International Patent Congress in Stockholm.
